list: The official 55 trophies, 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden. Names, descriptions and grades as PlayStation publishes them (Exophase / PSNProfiles, 18 Nov 2026). Guides in this file are the author's own words.

powerpyx.label: PowerPyx

powerpyx.role: Unlock methods and roadmap, retrieved 19 Nov 2026

trophies.guide: This is the last trophy you will earn: it pops the moment the other 54 are done, so there is no separate task to chase. Everything is single-player, with no online or DLC trophy standing between you and it, and one playthrough is enough because free-roam stays open after the credits. The real gate is the gold trophy A Long Road, which wants the 100% completion checklist finished; that checklist is closer to 60% of everything in the game, not a true 100%, and every item on it can still be done after the story. PowerPyx rates the whole set 4 out of 10 in difficulty and about 200 hours, with the story alone taking 60 to 80 hours. Keep cheats off the entire run: turning one on disables trophies and saving for that session.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Play the first main mission, Gone Fishing, in Chapter 1. It is the opening mission of the story, so you cannot miss it and there is nothing to prepare: follow the mission markers, finish the job, and the trophy pops at the end. PowerPyx lists it as an automatic story trophy. It is also the first step of the platinum, and it introduces Jason and Lucia and the Leonida setting. Because story missions cannot be replayed, keep a manual save at the start of each chapter (the game gives you 15 manual slots plus one autosave) in case you ever want to revisit a moment, but this trophy itself needs no special care.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1. The trophy unlocks when the chapter closes, which PowerPyx places just after the first mission of Chapter 2 begins (the chapter boundary falls there). Chapter 1 is where you should do the one thing in the game that might be missable: the meditation at Jason's house. After the Chapter 1 mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning, follow her to the balcony when she says she is going to meditate, and choose Accept. That meditation is the only one PowerPyx flags as possibly missable, so do it before you leave Chapter 1 even though the rest of the game can be cleaned up later.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 2. The trophy pops when the chapter ends, which PowerPyx places just after the first mission of Chapter 3 (Welcome to Vice City) begins. Chapter 2 is when the map really opens up and character switching unlocks: after the mission Coffee Break you can play as both Jason and Lucia, which is what lets you call your partner, meditate with both characters, and start several side questlines. Use the chapter to scan vehicles with the WAiNK app and study animals with the binoculars as you travel, because both feed the 100% checklist and the scanning counts from the moment you start, even before the checklist itself becomes visible after the story.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 3. The trophy unlocks when the chapter closes, just after the first two missions of Chapter 4 (Ocean Beach and Another Life) are done, according to PowerPyx. Chapter 3 is the busiest chapter for unlocking systems: the Key Cloner arrives with the mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs, the jewelry jobs open up with Yasmani, and several side characters (Andy, Randy, Tyrone) get their questlines marked. None of the chapter trophies can be missed, and the story keeps going in a straight line, so just keep playing the pink main-mission markers and the trophy will come.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 4. The trophy pops when the chapter ends, after the final Chapter 4 mission, Starting From Zero, according to PowerPyx. Chapter 4 is where the big robbery systems come online: the optional mission That's Where The Money Is introduces the large bank vault jobs, which are worth doing as they appear because each one pays up to $205,000 and they feed both the bank-vault trophy and the money-laundering total. You also get the armored-truck robbery here, which counts toward the same mission. As with the other chapter trophies, there is nothing missable about it: finish the missions and it unlocks.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Complete the final mission of the story. This is the only gold trophy tied to the story, and it unlocks at the credits. PowerPyx lists it as an automatic story trophy that cannot be missed. Once it pops, the game returns you to free-roam and the 100% completion checklist becomes visible under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion. Everything you did during the story already counts toward that checklist, so there is no need to hold anything back for after the credits. The story itself takes roughly 60 to 80 hours across its five chapters, and there is no mission replay, so keep a manual save at the start and end of each chapter if you want to revisit the finale later.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Play the main mission Breakfast Run in Chapter 2. It is a story mission, so it unlocks automatically as you follow the pink main-mission markers, and it cannot be missed. PowerPyx places it in Chapter 2 and lists it among the automatic story trophies. There is no special objective to watch for: there are no mission gold medals in this game, so you do not need to chase hidden objectives inside a mission. Just finish Breakfast Run and the trophy pops. If you are tracking the story trophies in order, this is one of the earlier ones, coming after the Chapter 2 opening.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Play the main mission The Cartel Heist in Chapter 3. It is a story mission, so it unlocks automatically when you finish it, and it cannot be missed. PowerPyx places it in Chapter 3 and lists it among the automatic story trophies. Like every story mission in this game, there is no gold-medal objective to worry about, so play it however you like and the trophy will pop at the end. The Cartel Heist is one of the bigger set-piece missions of the chapter, and it sits in the middle of the story, so you will reach it naturally by following the main missions after Chapter 2.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Play the main mission Child's Play in Chapter 4. It is a story mission, so it unlocks automatically when you finish it, and it cannot be missed. PowerPyx places it in Chapter 4 and lists it among the automatic story trophies. There are no mission medals to chase in this game, so there is no hidden objective inside Child's Play to prepare for. Just follow the mission through to its end. Chapter 4 is a long chapter with several mission trophies in it (Child's Play, Headliners, and the VCIA Takedown), so you will collect a few of these in a row as you work through it.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Play the main mission Headliners in Chapter 4. It is a story mission, so it unlocks automatically when you finish it, and it cannot be missed. PowerPyx places it in Chapter 4 and lists it among the automatic story trophies. There is no medal or side objective to worry about inside the mission: this game has no mission gold medals, so you can play Headliners at your own pace and the trophy pops at the end. It is one of three mission trophies in Chapter 4, alongside Child's Play and the VCIA Takedown, so expect a run of story trophies as you push through the chapter.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Play the main mission VCIA Takedown in Chapter 4. It is a story mission, so it unlocks automatically when you finish it, and it cannot be missed. PowerPyx places it in Chapter 4 and lists it among the automatic story trophies. The mission takes you to Vice City International Airport, which is worth remembering: the same airport is where you later steal a passenger plane for the Catch Me If You Can trophy, so you will already know the layout when you come back for that one. There is no hidden objective inside VCIA Takedown, so just finish the mission and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Play the main mission Operation Savage Glory in Chapter 5. It is a story mission, so it unlocks automatically when you finish it, and it cannot be missed. PowerPyx places it in Chapter 5 and lists it among the automatic story trophies. It is the last mission trophy before the finale, so by the time it pops you are nearly at the end of the story. There is no medal or hidden objective to chase inside it. Finish Operation Savage Glory, then play on to the final mission for the gold story trophy, and the game will drop you back into free-roam with the 100% checklist unlocked.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Finish the 100% completion checklist, which appears under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion only after the story ends. Progress you made during the story already counts, and nothing on the checklist is missable, so everything can be done in free-roam after the credits. PowerPyx stresses that the checklist is forgiving: it is closer to 60% of everything in the game, not a true 100%. You need any 100 optional missions (there are well over 200), 300 of the 397 stunts, 200 of 277 base-model vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied, 70 of 80 challenges, and 15 of 18 meditation spots. Only a few categories demand everything: all robberies, all underwater discoveries, all shooting ranges, all drone races, and all of Bret's target decks. Both PowerPyx and GTAbase call this the hardest trophy in the set, and it is the last big gate before the platinum.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Pull off any 250 of the 397 stunts scattered across Leonida. There are four kinds: 130 stunt jumps off ramps, 202 flights under bridges, 40 knife flights between buildings, and 25 base jumps with a parachute, and you can mix them however you like, so pick the easiest ones first. PowerPyx calls the under-bridge flights the quickest to knock out. For the 100% checklist you will eventually need 300 stunts, so keep going past 250 while you are at it. Track your progress by region under Progress, then Activities, then Stunts (press R3 on a category to see the regional split), or on the map under Exploration, then Stunt Spots, where every stunt has its own name and stays marked once you have done it. Performing a stunt once is enough to count it; the extra challenges shown on the map icons are optional.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Do each of the nine activity types at least once. The game tracks them under Touchpad, then Progress, then Activities, where scrolling over each type shows how many you have done. The nine are fishing, hunting, golf, shooting ranges, pool, basketball, playing a video game, winning a car race or drone race, and performing a stunt. Most of them are introduced automatically by the story, and the rest show up when you unfog the map: filter the map for Activities (the blue dumbbell icon) and the blue markers will point you at them. You will almost certainly finish this without trying, because working on the other trophies and the 100% checklist drags you through one of each anyway, so treat it as a free trophy that pops while you play.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every one of the 42 shooting range challenges, spread across 12 shooting range locations. PowerPyx lists all 12 locations and all 42 medals in its shooting range guide. Each challenge tests speed and accuracy with a different weapon, so use the range's own scoring to learn what gold demands: fast, clean hits beat spraying. The ranges also feed your Focus level, which makes the Gunslinger trophy easier later, so there is a double payoff for practicing here. Nothing about the ranges is missable, and they stay open after the story, so work through them at your own pace and come back for the ones that give you trouble once your aim and your weapons have improved.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations, which together host 42 drone races. PowerPyx lists every location in its drone race guide. The races are short flying courses, so learn each one by flying it once to see the gates, then race it properly for the win. You do not need to win every race at a location, just one win per location, which keeps the grind reasonable. The drone races also count toward the 100% checklist, so they are not optional work: the checklist wants them all done. They stay available after the story, so there is no rush, but they are a good early activity because they teach you the flying controls that the stunt and bridge flights will need later.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races from the 40 unique race locations PowerPyx lists. Any 20 will do, so pick the shortest and easiest circuits and learn their lines instead of grinding the hardest ones. Races include car races, race challenges, and the Top Fun drone races, so the wins you pick up for the drone trophy and for Master of None can count here too. There is no difficulty setting to worry about, and the races stay open after the story, so you can clean them up in free-roam. A good car matters more than a perfect line on most circuits: bring the fastest car you have, and do not be afraid to retry a race the moment you fall behind, because only wins count.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. The questline starts after the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui, where you meet Cal: some time after that mission, Cal sends a text that marks a fishing spot with a purple icon on the map, and following his fishing questline leads to the challenge. Fishing itself is one of the nine activity types, so this also feeds Master of None. There is no trick to the challenge beyond the fishing itself: cast, wait for the bite, and reel in with steady tension. Cal's challenge is a one-off, so once you beat him the trophy pops and you can move on. It stays available after the story, so if you miss the text early, keep playing and it will come.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish one of the four arcade games, which the game calls Video Games: Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III, Time Jackers Rewind, and Bang For Your Buck. The first three are playable on the TV at home by interacting with the controllers, and you can start as early as Chapter 1 (they are sometimes unavailable during certain story sections, but they open up again after the story). The fourth, Bang For Your Buck, is found at arcade machines out in the world. To complete a game you must finish all of its levels at least once; you do not need to beat every challenge inside it, just reach the end. Pick whichever game you enjoy most and play it through, and the trophy pops when you finish it.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's optional questline, which is marked automatically in Chapter 3 and is exclusive to Lucia. While playing as Lucia in Chapter 3 you will get a call from Andy, and then she texts you her home address, which marks the questline on the map in Belville. There are five quests to complete: Climbing the Cellerichain (in three parts), Pay the Cellerica Fee, Peach (join the Cellerica initiation), Read the Label (retrieve the Cellerica van), and Puff Puff Pass (meet at the warehouse). All of Andy's quests stay available after the story, so there is no deadline. Finish the last one and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's optional questline, which is marked automatically in Chapter 1. A while after the Chapter 1 mission Island Dreams, where you work for Kenton, he will call you, and then he is marked by the green KR icon in Key Lento. He offers sets of treasure-diving quests at shipwrecks: he marks purple treasure chest icons on the map, you dive down, use the metal detector to dig the treasure out of the ocean floor, and bring it back to him. After you turn in the first set he calls you back to his shop and then marks more locations; in total he wants you to clear seven shipwrecks. Track it under Progress, then Characters, then Kenton Rees, and under Progress, then Collections, then Kenton's Treasures. Kenton goes away for a while after Chapter 1 but comes back in Chapters 2 and 3, and as Jason you can speed it up by calling Brian later in Chapter 2, so the questline is not missable.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's optional questline, which is marked automatically after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, at the Thrillbilly Mudclub in Kelly County. There are five quests to complete: Thrillbillies (check out the mud club), Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab (join Billy on a job), Mall Rats (join Billy on a job), The Impaler (steal the Impaler), and Hometown Heroes (join Billy on a job). All of Billy's quests stay available after the story, so there is no deadline and nothing to miss. Work through them in order and the trophy pops when you finish the last one, Hometown Heroes.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight stranger mission strands, but note that only certain questlines count toward this trophy. PowerPyx is clear that many optional questlines do not count as strangers for this purpose: Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, Andy, Billy, and Eddie are all excluded, even though they feel like stranger missions. The ones confirmed to count are Kirk (the Skunk Ape quests: Search for the Skunk Ape, Search for Tree Effigies, and Help Kirk Find Mr. Mangrove), Kyle (Check Out McKittrick Farm, Collect Chemicals for Kyle, and Buddy?), Yago (Join a Street Race, Bumper to Bumper, Race Against Yago, and Brother to Brother), and Pilot Pete (The Last Mile quests and his deliveries). PowerPyx notes there are more strangers still to be found, so keep exploring. You can see how many you have finished on the trophy tracker, and all of them stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's optional questline, Randy's Wish List, which is marked automatically after the Chapter 3 mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs, where you steal the Zorrusso for Randy. That mission also unlocks the Key Cloner, which lets you break into high-end sports cars. Randy then gives you a list of 16 sports cars he wants delivered. Track them under Map, then Robberies, then Randy's Wish List: he marks some cars for you in fixed locations, but you can also steal them off the street, and when you scan or enter a car he wants you get a popup to deliver it to him. He is marked by the green RK icon in the west of Vice City. Scan high-end sports cars with the WAiNK app to check whether one is on the list, then drive it back to his garage; delivering it in good condition pays you more. The cars turn up most often in the east of Vice City around Vice Beach and Ocean Beach, parked outside hotels or driving around, and new locations get marked as you complete the ones he set. This can all be done after the story.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's optional questline, which is marked automatically after the Chapter 3 mission Here, Kitty Kitty, and is only available as Jason, not as Lucia. After that mission you will see purple markers for Synthetic Labs in Vice City: go to the labs and destroy them as part of the quest Take Out Kitty Litter. All of this stays available after the story. Once you have destroyed enough labs, Tyrone gives you his second quest, Spin On This, to shut down the labs, and finishing that quest unlocks the trophy. The two quests are Take Out Kitty Litter (the Kitty Litter labs) and Spin On This (shut down the labs).
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots, spread across 10 locations. You can meditate with both Lucia and Jason at each spot, and doing it with both counts as two meditations at the same location. Track your progress under Progress, then Collections, then Exploration, then Meditations. Do the Chapter 1 meditation first, because it is the one that might be missable: after the Chapter 1 mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning, follow her to the balcony when she says she is going to meditate, and choose Accept. That meditation is only available during Chapter 1 and is gone after the chapter ends, and it is still unclear whether it is required for the trophy, so do it to be safe. You cannot do the final meditation until you can play both characters together, which unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break. For the 100% checklist you only need 15 of the 18 spots, but this trophy wants all of them.
trophies.missableNote: Possibly missable: the Chapter 1 meditation at Jason's house is only available during Chapter 1. Do it before the chapter ends.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Collect all 3 of the Target Deck card sets.
trophies.guide: Collect all three Target Deck card sets, which is 15 Bret Target Decks in total. The questline starts after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, when Bret texts Jason and gives him the unique rifle Killtelligence SM-69. The first quest is Veteran Hunted: collect the Target Deck in Lummox County. After that, Bret keeps sending you to more decks, and each deck holds three cards, so you are collecting 45 cards across the 15 decks. Track your progress under Progress, then Collections, then Bret's Target Decks. The decks are spread all over Leonida, so treat it as a long-term collectible hunt and pick them up as you travel for other trophies. All of them stay available after the story.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Scan 100 locations with the WAiNK app. Open the app on your phone, aim at a vehicle or a marked location, and hold Up and then R1 to scan it. The WAiNK app is the game's way of logging everything you have found, and it ties into two trophies at once: this one for 100 locations and Whip It Good for 100 vehicles scanned. For the 100% checklist you will eventually need to scan 200 base-model vehicles, so the habit you build here pays off twice. Check how many you have found under Touchpad, then Progress, then Vehicles. There is no trick to it: just scan everything you drive past, especially in the busy parts of Vice City, and the count climbs fast.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete any 50 of the 80 challenges in the game. Challenges are the small tasks the game calls Activities in other titles, and they cover everything from driving and shooting to the side systems, so you will rack them up naturally as you play. For the 100% checklist you will eventually need 70 of the 80, so keep going past 50 while you are at it. There is no single list of all 80 in one place, but the game shows each challenge's progress as you work on it, and the ones tied to the main activities (stunts, races, shooting ranges) are the easiest to find. Just play broadly, try everything once, and the trophy will pop well before you have finished the rest of the game.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Escape a 4-star wanted level while on a date.
trophies.guide: Escape a 4-star wanted level while you are on a date with your partner. After the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break you can call your partner by pressing Right and then Triangle on the phone, which starts a date. Then get yourself a 4-star wanted level and escape it. PowerPyx recommends escaping through the train tunnel north of Ambrosia in Kelly County, which breaks line of sight and lets the heat die down. If you would rather not set it up yourself, this also unlocks automatically during the Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is, where the same situation happens as part of the story. Either way, the key is to be on a date when you escape the wanted level.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Shop at 3 stores back-to-back while wanted.
trophies.guide: Go shopping with your partner at three stores back-to-back while you are wanted. After the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, call your partner and then get a wanted level, and keep it while you visit three shops in a row. PowerPyx recommends three jewelry stores in the north of Vice City, which become a good route after the Chapter 3 Yasmani jewelry jobs. The wanted level needs to stay active (the red and blue flashing) while you go from shop to shop, and the trophy pops about 30 seconds after you leave the third shop, so do not worry if it does not fire the instant you walk out. Bring your partner, keep the heat on, and shop three times in a row.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Scan 100 vehicles with the WAiNK app. Open the app on your phone, aim at a vehicle, and hold Up and then R1 to scan it. For the 100% checklist you will eventually need to scan 200 of the 277 base-model vehicles, so this trophy is really the first half of a longer job. Check how many you have found under Touchpad, then Progress, then Vehicles. The fastest way to rack up scans is to walk through the busy parts of Vice City and scan everything parked and driving past, because the game counts each base model once. New vehicles keep appearing as you travel, so keep the app open and scan as you go, and the trophy will pop long before you hit 200.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Kill 5 enemies in one Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Kill five enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Activate Combat Focus by pressing L3 and R3 together while you are aiming, which slows time and sharpens your aim. There are four focus levels, and the higher your focus the longer it lasts, so build it up first: eat food, drink, and wash your character to raise focus, and use Adrenaline to extend it once it is active. Gang operations are the best place to try this, because they give you a group of enemies in a small area, and the Duke 556 assault rifle is a good weapon for it. Note that it does not work on soldiers, police, or civilians: it has to be five proper enemies in one focus window. If you run out of time, just try again at the next gang operation.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. After the Chapter 3 Yasmani jewelry jobs you get access to the Snap Gun, which lets you enter through the back door silently. The store to hit is Richardson Jewelry and Diamonds in Vice City. Go in through the back with the Snap Gun, find the safe code note inside, and get out without tripping the alarm or being seen. The key is patience: move slowly, use cover, and do not rush the safe. If you are spotted, back out and try again, because the store stays open and the trophy only counts a clean run. Do it after the Yasmani jobs so you have the Snap Gun, and the job is much easier.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults. The vault jobs open up after the Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is, which introduces the large bank vault system. After that mission you can tail a security van to a bank, and you need to bring your partner along to carry a bag. Yasmani sells van tips for $10,000 after you finish his Payday Loans quests, which makes finding the vans much easier. There are eight large bank vaults in total, and each one can pay up to $205,000, so they are worth doing for the money as well as the trophy. You only need five for the trophy, but all eight count toward the 100% checklist, so do them all. Expect a four-star wanted level the moment you start, and plan your escape route before you go in.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck. This is the same job as the vault robberies: it opens up after the Chapter 4 optional mission That's Where The Money Is. You can either do it as part of that mission, where the vault robbery counts, or find an armored truck on its own: block it, use a sticky bomb on the back door to blow it open, and then escape the red heat radius that appears around the truck. PowerPyx notes this is a nod to the classic blitz play from GTA III, which is where the trophy's name comes from. The truck robbery is quick once you know the trick, and the money inside is worth having, so it is a good job to do while you are working on the bank vaults.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Fully unfog the map of Leonida. The map starts fogged, and every area you visit clears the fog around it, so the job is simply to travel everywhere. PowerPyx recommends doing it by plane, because flying covers the map much faster than driving, and you can see the fog lifting as you go. The best time to do it is after the story, when the whole map is open and you are already travelling for the collectibles and the 100% checklist. There is nothing missable about it: the fog clears permanently as you visit each area, and the trophy pops the moment the last patch of fog disappears. It pairs well with the stunts and the vehicle scanning, since you will be visiting the same remote corners anyway.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Clear one gang operation for each of the 9 gangs.
trophies.guide: Clear one gang operation for each of the nine gangs in Leonida. There are 39 gang operations in total, shown as yellow icons on the map, and you only need one per gang for this trophy, but all 39 count toward the 100% checklist, so you will be doing them all eventually. Track your progress under Progress, then Gangs, which shows how many operations you have cleared for each gang. Gang operations are also a good place to work on the Gunslinger trophy, because they give you a group of enemies in a small area, and they pay well. Pick the easiest operation for each gang first, clear one for all nine, and the trophy pops. Then keep going for the full 39.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 in marked bills. After the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check you get the Dye Pack Jammer, which lets you rob banks and Payday Loans stores and take the marked bills, and then you bring those bills to a fence to clean them. Yasmani pays the most for marked bills, so he is the best fence to use. The total is cumulative across the whole game, so every bank and Payday Loans robbery adds to it, and the vault jobs are the fastest way to rack up large amounts because each vault can pay up to $205,000. You do not need to do it all at once: just keep robbing and laundering as you play, and the trophy pops when your lifetime total passes $250,000.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across the shops of Leonida. The total is cumulative, so everything you buy counts: guns, car mods, tattoos, clothes, and more. PowerPyx says the fastest way to spend it is on guns, car modifications, and tattoos, which are the most expensive items. There are plenty of shops to spend it in: 14 mod shops, 19 Pay 'n' Sprays, 24 Ammu-Nations, 67 clothing stores, 17 footwear shops, 18 hair and beauty salons, 11 tattoo parlours, and 15 electronics stores. You will spend a lot of this naturally while playing, because weapons and car upgrades are expensive, so the trophy often pops on its own. If you are short at the end, buy the most expensive car mod or weapon you can afford and the total will tip over $100,000.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy eight garages. There are eight purchasable garages in total, plus four story garages that do not count toward this trophy, and together the eight cost $160,000. They become available after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver, and you buy them through the Vice City Real Estate app on your phone. The garages are not just a trophy: you need them for the On the Spot trophy, because the Scooter Bros app needs a parking spot before it will let you register a stolen vehicle. Buy them as you can afford them, and the trophy pops when you own all eight. The money is worth spending, because the garages also give you somewhere to store the cars you collect for Randy's wish list.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.guide: Register ten stolen vehicles through the Scooter Bros app. The app opens up after the Chapter 2 Moses mission, and you need to own garages first, because the app needs a parking spot before it will let you register anything. Drive a stolen vehicle to Moses in Port Gellhorn, then choose Respray and Register to make it yours. At first you can only register cars without trackers, but later you can fit standard trackers at a Pay 'n' Spray, which opens up more cars. Register ten vehicles in total and the trophy pops. It is a good way to build a collection of cars, and it pairs well with the vehicle scanning and the garage buying, since you need the garages anyway.
trophies.name: On the Spot

trophies.description: Steal a passenger plane from VCIA.
trophies.guide: Steal a large passenger plane from Vice City International Airport. The easiest planes to take are the ones docked at a departure terminal, and PowerPyx says gates E3 and E4 are the easiest to reach. Go upstairs into the terminal, find the cockpit, and drive the plane backwards onto the airstrip before you take off. Once you are in the air, fly at least one kilometre away from the airport and the trophy pops. The airport is the same place you visited for the VCIA Takedown mission, so you will already know the layout. Do not worry about the wanted level: once you are airborne and away from the airport, the heat will die down on its own.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Steal a tank from Mile Zero Air Station, on the south-west island in Mariana County. PowerPyx says the tanks are parked in the south of the base, so enter from the south side and look for them there. The base is guarded, so expect a fight on the way in, and once you are in the tank, drive it out and get away from the base. A tank is slow but nearly unstoppable, so the hard part is getting to it, not getting away in it. Once you have stolen the tank and driven it clear of the base, the trophy pops. Do it after the story when you are well armed, and the guards will be much less of a problem.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Find the beginning of the story.
trophies.guide: This trophy's trigger has not been confirmed yet. PowerPyx lists it as currently unknown, and no reliable method has been published as of 19 November 2026. That means this guide cannot give you a step-by-step method without guessing, and guessing would waste your time. What is known is that it is a bronze trophy in the activities group, and that it is not tied to the story missions, because the story trophies are all accounted for. The best advice for now is to keep playing and checking back: the community is still working on it, and a method will be published once someone finds it. This guide will be updated as soon as a confirmed trigger is known.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.unconfirmedNote: Unconfirmed: PowerPyx lists the trigger as currently unknown. No reliable method has been published yet.

trophies.description: Steal the blue Banshee from the showroom.
trophies.guide: Steal the blue Banshee from the car showroom in the south of Vice City. You need the Key Cloner first, which you unlock in the Chapter 3 mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' Gs, because the Banshee is locked and the Key Cloner is what lets you break into high-end sports cars. Once you have the Key Cloner, go to the showroom, find the blue Banshee, and drive it straight through the showroom window to get it out. PowerPyx notes this is a nod to the classic GTA III mission where you steal a Banshee the same way, which is where the trophy's name comes from. Once you have driven it out of the showroom, the trophy pops, and the Banshee is yours to keep.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Steal all 3 key valuables from Kingpin Bowling.
trophies.guide: Steal all three key valuables from Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn, which is a gang operation. The three valuables are a luxury watch in the south-east office, the Gutterball Moreland 850 shotgun on a table in the north-east, and the safe in the north-east hallway office, which you need to blow open with sticky bombs. The gang operation is introduced by the Chapter 2 optional mission Hit Kingpin Bowling, and the trophy unlocks after you escape the police with all three valuables. The valuables respawn later if you miss one, so this is not missable: you can come back and try again. Clear the gang operation, grab all three valuables, escape the police, and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Let's Go Bowling

trophies.description: Reach maximum strength with both Jason and Lucia.
trophies.guide: Reach maximum strength with both Jason and Lucia at the same time. You can check each character's strength under Touchpad, then Jason and Lucia, then Strength. The way to build strength is to work out at the fitness clubs, and you need to do it with both characters, because the trophy only pops when both of them are at maximum at once. You can start after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, when you can play as both characters. The fastest way is to work out with both characters together at a fitness club, doing the same exercises, until both of their strength bars are full. It takes a while, but it is straightforward, and the trophy pops the moment both characters hit maximum.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Perform 500 criminal-profile actions. The game tracks your criminal profile, and you can see how many actions you have done on the trophy itself. There are five profiles the game can give you, from Professional up to Irredeemable, and PowerPyx warns that Irredeemable is permanent, so avoid the actions that push you toward it. The 500 actions happen naturally as you play: every crime you commit, from stealing cars to robbing stores to fighting the police, adds to the count. You do not need to grind it, because by the time you have finished the story and the 100% checklist you will be well past 500. Just keep playing, and the trophy pops on its own.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.description: Get unlucky at the Payday Loans store.
trophies.guide: This trophy's trigger has not been confirmed yet. PowerPyx lists it as currently unknown, and says it is believed to be related to the Payday Loans store from the prologue, but that is a guess, not a confirmed method. That means this guide cannot give you a step-by-step method without guessing, and guessing would waste your time. What is known is that it is a bronze trophy in the activities group, and that the Payday Loans stores are the places where you rob marked bills for the money-laundering trophy, so you will be visiting them anyway. The best advice for now is to keep playing, rob the Payday Loans stores as part of the money-laundering work, and check back: a method will be published once someone finds it. This guide will be updated as soon as a confirmed trigger is known.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.unconfirmedNote: Unconfirmed: PowerPyx lists the trigger as currently unknown; it is believed to be related to the Payday Loans store from the prologue, but that is not confirmed.

trophies.guide: This trophy's trigger has not been confirmed yet. PowerPyx reports a possible UFO method: go to the road north-west of the Starlet Motel in Kelly County after 2AM, alone, and look for a blinking car, then follow the path into the woods, where a UFO drops a woman. But that method has not been confirmed, and this guide labels it as unconfirmed rather than presenting it as a fact. If you want to try it, go to that road after 2AM on your own and look for the blinking car, but do not be surprised if nothing happens. The community is still working on this one, and a confirmed method will be published once someone finds it. This guide will be updated as soon as a confirmed trigger is known.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.unconfirmedNote: Unconfirmed: PowerPyx reports a possible UFO method (road NW of Starlet Motel, Kelly County, after 2AM, solo, blinking car, follow the path into the woods), but it is not confirmed.

trophies.guide: Hunt the animal Bret wants. Bret's questline starts after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, when Bret texts Jason and gives him the unique rifle Killtelligence SM-69. The first quest is Veteran Hunted: collect the Target Deck in Lummox County, which is also the start of the card-collecting trophy. Bret is a hunting questline, and the animal you need to hunt for this trophy is the part that has not been confirmed yet: PowerPyx says it is still undergoing confirmation which animal exactly unlocks this trophy. That means this guide cannot name the animal without guessing. The best advice is to follow Bret's questline, hunt the animals he points you at, and check back: the exact animal will be published once someone confirms it. This guide will be updated as soon as the animal is known.
trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.unconfirmedNote: Unconfirmed: PowerPyx says it is still undergoing confirmation which animal exactly unlocks this trophy.

trophies.description: Knock down 10 enemies with a motorcycle.
trophies.guide: This trophy's trigger has not been confirmed yet. PowerPyx lists it as currently unknown, and says it is believed to be from kicking enemies while driving a motorcycle, but that is a guess, not a confirmed method. That means this guide cannot give you a step-by-step method without guessing, and guessing would waste your time. What is known is that it is a bronze trophy in the activities group, and that it is likely tied to motorcycle combat, so riding a motorcycle and fighting enemies from it is a reasonable thing to try while you play. The best advice for now is to keep playing, try kicking enemies while riding a motorcycle, and check back: a method will be published once someone finds it. This guide will be updated as soon as a confirmed trigger is known.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.unconfirmedNote: Unconfirmed: PowerPyx lists the trigger as currently unknown; it is believed to be from kicking enemies while driving a motorcycle, but that is not confirmed.
